newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Reunert shares slip on flat results.
newsitem.headline: Reunert shares slip on flat results.

text.p: Shares in South African electronics and telecommunications group Reunert Ltd slipped in early trade on Wednesday as the market digested disappointing results.

Late on Tuesday the group posted a slight rise in pre-exceptional earnings per share for the year to September 30 to 104.1 cents from 103.4 cents. The group's shares slipped 55 cents to 17.75 rand by 0825 GMT.
"All in all in the market was expecting a little bit more," one analyst said.

Reunert said the results were hit by the slow delivery of South African telecommunications infrastructure. The firm added that caution was needed when considering next year's prospects due to uncertainty over the appointment of an international equity partner for parastatal Telkom.
Analysts said the short-term outlook for the group was a little bleak and investors looking for quick returns in the sector should switch stock to groups like Plessey.
However, the longer term outlook could be much brighter if the Telkom partner is successfully announced. Reunert would stand to reap benefits from the overseas exposure that would bring.
"In the longer term if something like Telkom comes off then Reunert will be very exposed to that," one analyst said.
On November 5 finance minister Trevor Manuel said he hoped the partial privatisation of Telkom would be completed within the fiscal year ending March 31.
Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom, Telekom Malaysia and South Western Bell have been shortlisted as potential strategic equity partners for Telkom.
